# Solved cases: start here

Every problem the agent has solved, with its verdict and report. The same reports, as a gallery:
[tomyud1.github.io/agentic-cfd](https://tomyud1.github.io/agentic-cfd/). The next problems are in
[BACKLOG.md](BACKLOG.md).

Each case was given to a **fresh agent** that had never seen it, with only the problem statement,
the tools and the guidelines. Its lessons were then folded back into the guidelines before the next
case.

<!-- /catalogue:solved -->

**PASS** means every check passed. **WARN** means the answer is usable but a check the agent set for
itself, before seeing the results, did not fully pass. **FAIL** means a requested output missed the
accuracy rule fixed before the runs. The report says which check and why. Verdicts are never
softened.

This table, the [backlog](BACKLOG.md) and the [gallery](../index.html) are generated from one list,
[`catalogue.yaml`](catalogue.yaml), by [`cfdlib/catalogue.py`](../cfdlib/catalogue.py). Verdicts are
read from each report's own results file. When a case is solved, change its entry in
`catalogue.yaml` to `status: solved` and run `python -m cfdlib.catalogue`.

## What is in every report

| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Summary | The answer to each requested output (lettered a, b, c...), key findings, limitations |
| 1 Problem | The problem in short, what we want to find, the setup, a sketch, the given data |
| 2 Assumptions | Each one with how it was checked (tested, standard, imposed by the model, or violated) |
| 3 Theory | What can be known without simulating: exact solution (SymPy) or scaling, limits and conservation laws |
| 4 Decisions | Every OpenFOAM setting, grouped into decisions with why, effect and alternatives. A checker refuses to render the report if any setting is undocumented |
| 5 Pre-flight | Short test runs before the long ones: crashes, stability, projected run time |
| 6 Simulation | The model, mesh and time-step studies, run health |
| 7 Comparison | Verification (exact solution) or validation (benchmark) with error bands and observed order of accuracy |
| 8 Insights | A live lab notebook: every problem the agent met, how it solved it and what should change in the workflow |
| 9 Reproducibility | The exact commands, files and software versions |
| Appendix | Optional studies, such as performance (case 4: MPI scaling, linear solvers, what limits speed) |

Some cases add a separate study report, such as the GPU vs CPU study of case 5 (what is compared,
the method, results per mesh size, the same-answer check, where the time goes, the insights).

## What is in a case folder

```
cases/<case>/
  problem.yaml                the problem statement (the only input the agent gets)
  reference/                  benchmark data with citations (when the case has a benchmark)
  numerics.yaml               the agent's numerical plan (meshes, time steps, tolerances)
  decisions.yaml              every choice, with why / effect / alternatives
  insights.yaml               the live insight log
  template/                   the OpenFOAM case (0/, constant/, system/) with {{ placeholders }}
  theory.py / analytical.py   theory (SymPy)
  run.py, analyze.py          run the simulations; analyse and write the report
  sketch.py                   the problem sketch
results/<case>/               report.html, results.json and the extracted run data (runs/)
```

## What each solved case shows

For an agent (or a person) choosing a case to study. Every folder is a complete record of how one
problem was solved: the plan, the decisions, the code and the insight log of the agent that solved
it. Nobody has to read them all. Open the ones close to your problem, or the one that shows a
technique you need. Copy structure and technique, not numerical settings.

<!-- catalogue:examples -->
<!-- generated by cfdlib/catalogue.py from cases/catalogue.yaml: edit that file, then run python -m cfdlib.catalogue -->

- **`cases/plane_poiseuille/`** (case 1, Steady, linear, exact solution). The smallest complete case: every file a case needs. Exact solution derived and self-checked with SymPy; verification against it.
- **`cases/lid_driven_cavity_re100/`** (case 2, Steady, nonlinear, benchmark (Ghia et al. 1982)). No exact solution: what theory can still say; comparison with a published benchmark; Richardson extrapolation; SIMPLEC stopped on residuals; separate pre-flight and production commands.
- **`cases/stokes_first_problem/`** (case 3, Transient, linear, exact solution). Transient: combined and separate mesh and time-step studies; a momentum balance checked at every step; several runs at once.
- **`cases/dfg_cylinder_re100/`** (case 4, Transient, nonlinear, vortex shedding, benchmark (FeatFlow)). Vortex shedding: curved-body O-grid mesh generated in Python; a benchmark with several reference levels; a live stop rule for a periodic flow; MPI runs and a performance appendix; the same case on gpucfd, with equal cells and with cells clustered around the cylinder (gpu_run.py, gpu_compare.py, gpu_clustered.py), and a study report built from recorded runs that sets the two solvers side by side (gpu_study.py). Key lesson: PISO was first order in time.
- **`cases/dfg_cylinder_3d_re20/`** (case 5, Steady, 3D, up to 2.4 million cells, benchmark (FeatFlow)). 3D: O-grid extruded with wall grading; a second mesh family for a sensitive output (lift); a GPU vs CPU performance study with its own report (gpu_study.py, OGL tuning, timing by profiling).
- **`cases/heated_pipe_re200/`** (case 6, Steady, first heat transfer, exact solution (thermal entrance series)). Heat transfer (buoyantBoussinesqSimpleFoam) on an axisymmetric wedge; an exact series solution checked by an independent method; extraction bias measured on the exact solution; buoyancy tested with a same-mesh on/off pair in 3D.

<!-- /catalogue:examples -->

To find out whether a problem was met before, search the insight logs: `grep -il "<keyword>"
cases/*/insights.yaml`.

## Give the agent a new problem

1. Open this repository in a coding agent ([Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), Codex or
   any other) and tell it to start from [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md).
2. Describe your problem in your own words: *"Solve this flow problem with the agentic-cfd workflow:
   ..."*. Give it:
   - what you want to find, and how accurate it must be, if you know;
   - the geometry and its dimensions;
   - the fluid and its properties;
   - the conditions at the inlet, outlet and walls (and the starting state, if the flow changes in
     time);
   - optionally, data to compare against (an exact solution, a benchmark, measurements) and its
     source.

The agent turns your description into a problem statement (`cases/<name>/problem.yaml`), asks
about anything missing, and starts once you confirm it. It then follows the workflow, logs insights
as it goes, and finishes with `results/<name>/report.html`. The cases here used Claude Opus 5.5 with
high effort; a case took from about 25 minutes (case 3) to about 2 hours (case 5, including the GPU
study).

To re-run a solved case, follow the commands in its report's **Reproducibility** section (machine
setup: [setup/README.md](../setup/README.md)).
